channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Euro: OAT repricing keeps downside bias against US Dollar – MUFG
item.description: Halpenny argues that last week’s sharp widening of the OAT/Bund spread to 150 bps looked overdone, with French bonds now retracing from oversold levels as global fixed income selling eases. He sees Marine Le Pen’s aggressive consolidation plan as unlikely to materially change OAT risk ahead of next year’s election. MUFG expects EUR/USD downside risks to prevail.

item.title: WTI eases as Gulf export flows counter Middle East, US storm concerns
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) oil price declines after paring its daily gains, trading around $89.00 per barrel during European hours on Wednesday.

item.title: Polish Zloty: NBP cautious as inflation overshoots – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Tatha Ghose highlights that Poland’s National Bank (NBP) is expected to keep its base rate at 3.75% in October, with guidance from Thursday’s press conference key. Several MPC members now see scope for rate hikes if projections show inflation above 4% next year.

item.title: Indian Rupee approaches all-time low around 97 after RBI's hawkish policy decision
item.description: The Indian Rupee ((INR) weakens significantly against the US Dollar (USD) after a muted response, following the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) monetary policy meeting on Wednesday. The USD/INR pair jumps to near 96.80, the highest level seen in four months.

item.title: Euro tumbles after a relief rally as ECB officials warn economic slowdown
item.description: The Euro (EUR) underperforms its major currency peers on Wednesday, trading almost 0.55% lower at around 177.00 against the Japanese Yen (JPY) in the European trade.

item.title: British Pound stays weak below 1.3250 as USD bulls retain control ahead of FOMC Minutes
item.description: The GBP/USD pair weakens further below mid-1.3200s during the first half of the European session on Wednesday, eroding a major part of the previous day's move higher amid a broadly firmer US Dollar (USD).

item.title: Japanese Yen edges up from lows amid hawkish comments from BoJ’s Sato
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) holds marginal gains against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday.

item.title: Dow Jones futures fall as US Treasury yields rebound ahead of FOMC Minutes
item.description: Dow Jones futures decline by 0.14% to trade near 51,750 during European hours on Wednesday. S&P 500 futures remain steady around 7,870, while Nasdaq 100 futures fall by 0.18% to trade near 31,430.

item.title: Czech Koruna: CNB path lifted on inflation risks – Standard Chartered
item.description: Standard Chartered’s Saabir Salad now expects the Czech National Bank to deliver two additional 25bps hikes, in November 2026 and Q1-2027, after a pre-emptive move in June. This would lift cumulative tightening to 75bps and the policy rate to 4.25% by end-Q1-2027.

item.title: Gold seems vulnerable near two-month low amid bullish USD; focus remains on FOMC Minutes
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) sticks to modest intraday losses through the first half of the European session on Wednesday, trading just above the two-month low around $4,100 touched the previous day. The US Dollar (USD) attracts fresh buyers and reverses a part of Tuesday's corrective slide.

item.title: Euro falls against Canadian Dollar as surging oil prices overpower strong German data
item.description: EUR/CAD continues its losing streak for the third successive day, trading around 1.5920 during the European hours on Wednesday. The currency cross is under downward pressure as the Euro (EUR) faces headwinds despite a stronger-than-expected rebound in German industrial performance.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Losses seem capped against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank (UOB) strategists Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note that USD/JPY traded on a firm footing in early Asian trade as upward momentum continued to build.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD ticks lower to near $60.60 as US bond yields bounce back
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) is slightly down to near $60.60 during the European trading session on Wednesday. The white metal faces marginal selling pressure as United States (US) Treasury Yields regain ground after a corrective move the previous day.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar declines as US Dollar strengthens on rising Treasury yields
item.description: NZD/USD depreciates after registering modest gains the previous day, trading around 0.5610 during the European hours on Wednesday.

item.title: Australian Dollar pulls back from one-week top as USD stays firm ahead of FOMC Minutes
item.description: The AUD/USD pair attracts some sellers on Wednesday, stalling a three-day recovery move from the 0.6900 neighborhood, or a three-month low, touched last week.

item.title: US Dollar: Lower yields pressure USD as December hike looms - Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank strategist Molly Schwartz notes US Treasury yields fell across the curve, pressuring the US Dollar (USD) even as the US Dollar Index (DXY) stays close to 102. She highlights evolving Fed communication and multiple officials stressing inflation risks from AI, tariffs and energy.

item.title: Gold: Central banks keep buying – ING
item.description: ING’s commodities team, led by Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey, reports that Gold edged higher on Tuesday as lower Oil prices and stronger bond markets eased inflation concerns and reduced expectations of further rate hikes. They emphasize persistent central bank demand, with World Gold Council data showing continued net buying driven by long-term reserve diversification.

item.title: EUR/GBP Price Forecast: Rejection at 0.8500 leaves yearly low at 0.8455 exposed
item.description: The Euro (EUR) extends losses against the British Pound (GBP) on Wednesday, on track to complete a nearly 1.6% decline in a nine-day losing streak.

item.title: Euro: Fiscal concerns limit recovery against US Dollar - Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Antje Praefcke notes that concerns over France’s national debt have recently weighed on the Euro, reviving memories of the earlier sovereign debt crisis.

item.title: British Pound: Upside capped near 1.3315 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank (UOB) strategists Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann report that GBP/USD broke above their prior resistance level as the British Pound (GBP) outperformed on Tuesday, invalidating an earlier mildly bearish view.

item.title: Canadian Dollar loses ground ahead of FOMC Minutes
item.description: The USD/CAD pair gathers strength to around 1.4220 during the early European trading hours on Wednesday. All eyes will be on the Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) later in the day for signals on a potential rate hike.

item.title: Japanese Yen: BoJ normalisation supports gains against US Dollar – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Michael Wan highlights that USD/JPY is still trading above 158, but Governor Ueda’s comments point to further Bank of Japan (BoJ) policy normalisation. Ueda stressed anchoring inflation around 2% and noted upside risks from imports, AI demand and JPY weakness.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar stabilizes as bond yields recover ahead of FOMC Minutes
item.description: Here is what you need to know on Wednesday, October 7:

item.title: Equities: Valuation reset underpins new highs – Danske Bank
item.description: Danske Research Team observes US equities extending their rebound, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq posting fresh record highs and cyclical laggards leading gains. The team argues markets are not excessively optimistic, noting valuation multiples have compressed over the past year and quarter.

item.title: Euro extends its reversal as rising Oil prices offset upbeat German data
item.description: The Euro (EUR) heads south against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday, giving away Tuesday's gains weighed by rising Oil prices and broad-based US Dollar strength ahead of the release of the minutes of the last Federal Reserve (Fed) meeting.

item.title: Oil: Supply risks offset stronger flows – ING
item.description: ING analysts Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey note that Oil supplies from the Persian Gulf are improving, but ICE Brent remains supported above $100/bbl as ongoing attacks on ships keep regional supply risks elevated.

item.title: US Dollar Index Price Forecast: 101.80 remains key support zone ahead of FOMC minutes
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) trades higher against its major peers ahead of the release of Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) minutes of the September policy meeting at 18:00 GMT.

item.title: Euro: Rebound capped by resistance against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank (UOB) strategists Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann highlight that EUR/USD bounced on Tuesday as the US Dollar Index (DXY) slipped, but they still see the broader Euro (EUR) downtrend intact.

item.title: Japan’s Takaichi to review policies, revenue and spending if rate shifts differ from expectations
item.description: Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae said on Wednesday that the government will consider reviewing policies, revenue, and spending if interest rate shifts differ from expectations.

item.title: 2.0%: Germany's Industrial Production rises faster-than-expected in August
item.description: Industrial Output, in the Eurozone’s economic powerhouse, climbed by 2.0% over the month in August, the federal statistics authority Destatis showed on Wednesday in figures adjusted for seasonal and calendar effects.
